name.description: The name the client supplied when pairing.

NativePairStatus.description:
Native (punktfunk/1) pairing status. Unlike GameStream, the **host** mints the PIN (the SPAKE2
ceremony needs it client-side first), so the console **displays** `pin` for the user to enter on
their device — armed on demand for a short window.

armed.description: True while a pairing window is open.

enabled.description: Whether the native host is running (the unified host started with `--native`).

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds left in the window (null = disarmed, or armed with no expiry via the CLI flag).

pin.description: The PIN to display while armed (null when disarmed).

hidden.description:
The operator hid this title ([`set_entry_hidden`]) — omitted when false, so the shape only
grows for entries that actually are hidden.

OperatorGameEntry.description:
A library entry plus the operator's own view of it — today, whether they hid it.

A separate type rather than a field on [`GameEntry`] for two reasons. It keeps the visibility
answer out of the providers entirely: a store parser has no opinion on what the operator hid, and
adding `hidden: false` to all eight construction sites would imply it does. More importantly it
makes the lane rule a TYPE guarantee instead of a discipline — `GET /library` answers
`Vec<GameEntry>` on every lane but the operator's, so a hidden entry cannot leak to a paired
client by someone forgetting a filter; there is no field there to leak.

`flatten` keeps the wire shape identical to a plain entry with one extra key, so the console
parses one model either way.

fingerprint.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the client certificate DER — the client's stable id here.

label.description:
Operator-assigned display name for this device, if one has been set (`PATCH /clients/{fp}`).

This is the ONLY thing that can tell two paired Moonlight devices apart in a list, because
their certificates cannot: see [`Self::subject`]. Absent until somebody names the device.

subject.description:
Certificate subject (e.g. `CN=NVIDIA GameStream Client`), if the DER parses.

Do not display this as a device name. Every moonlight-common-c client self-signs with that
same fixed subject, so it identifies the *protocol*, not the device — a list of paired
phones, TVs and handhelds all read identically. [`Self::label`] is the field to show.

pin_pending.description: True while a pairing handshake is parked waiting for the user's PIN.

PendingDevice.description:
An unpaired device that tried to connect while the host requires pairing — awaiting
**delegated approval** (approve it here instead of fetching the host PIN out of band).

access_level.description:
The stored mask's preset name (`full` | `controller` | `view` | `custom`) — `null` for a
device with no stored record, unlike [`NativeClient`] where it is always derivable.

age_secs.description: Seconds since the device last knocked.

expires_unix.description:
The stored record's absolute expiry (unix seconds; likely in the past — that's why it's
knocking). `null` when unknown or permanent.

fingerprint.description: Hex SHA-256 of the device's certificate — what approval pins.

granted_unix.description: When the stored record's access was granted (unix seconds). `null` when unknown.

grants.description:
The grant mask this fingerprint is ALREADY stored with, if it was paired before (the
expired-guest re-knock: the approve dialog can offer "re-grant what they had"). `null`
when the device is unknown, or known with a pre-grants record (= full).

id.description: Id to address approve/deny (per-process; entries expire after ~10 minutes).

name.description: Best-effort device label (the client's own name, else fingerprint-derived).

Plane.description:
Which protocol plane an event originated from. Hooks and scripts filter on it — a hook
that fires for native clients but not Moonlight clients is a bug, not a v2 feature.

PluginLogBatch.description: A batch of runner log lines.

PluginLogLine.description: One log line produced by the runner or a plugin inside it (`POST /plugins/logs`).

source.description:
Which unit emitted it — a plugin's `definePlugin` name, a package name, or `runner`.
Surfaced in the console's target column as `plugin:<source>`.

ts_ms.description:
When the line was produced, unix milliseconds. Kept verbatim — see
[`crate::log_capture::LogRing::push_remote`].

category.description:
What KIND of plugin this is (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`), top-level rather than under `ui`
because it describes the plugin, not its surface. The console knows one value today —
`library` — which it filters **out of the nav**: six installed scanner plugins would otherwise
flood the sidebar, and their real entry point is the Game sources surface (design D5). A
library plugin that genuinely wants its own page (rom-manager, which is much more than a
scanner) simply omits the category.

title.description: Human-readable title for the console nav entry (1–64 chars; control chars stripped).

oneOf.description:
Present iff the plugin serves a UI surface. A registration with no `ui` is a liveness/phone-book
entry only (e.g. a future runner-management listing) and grows no nav entry.

version.description: Optional plugin version, purely informational (≤32 chars).

PluginSummary.description:
One entry in `GET /plugins`. **Never carries the secret** — the browser learns a plugin exists
and has a UI, nothing that lets it reach the plugin directly (it goes through the console proxy).

PluginUi.description:
A plugin's UI surface as it registers it. Carries the secret — this shape is only ever a request
body, never a response ([`PluginUiPublic`] is the secret-free view).

icon.description: Optional lucide icon name for the console nav entry (`^[a-z0-9-]{1,48}$`).

port.description:
The **loopback** port the plugin serves its UI on. The host and console only ever dial
`127.0.0.1:<port>`; a registration can never carry a hostname.

secret.description:
Per-boot shared secret the console proxy must present (as `Authorization: Bearer`) on every
request to the plugin's UI server. Rotated whenever the plugin restarts.

PluginUiPublic.description: The secret-free view of a plugin's UI surface — what [`list_plugins`] returns to the browser.

PortMap.description:
Every port a client integration may need (Moonlight derives the stream ports from the
HTTP base; a control pane should not have to).

Position.description: A desktop-space offset for a display (top-left origin).

PrepCmd.description:
One per-app preparation step (RFC §6 — deliberate Sunshine `prep-cmd` parity): `do` runs
**synchronously before the app launches** (an HDR toggle or a MangoHud env change must land
first), `undo` runs at session end — reverse order across steps, best-effort, on every exit
path including a crash-unwind (RAII via [`PrepGuard`]).

do.description:
Command run before launch. Same execution recipe and ownership checks as hook `run`
commands (event-less: stdin is empty JSON, env carries the `PF_APP_*` context).

undo.description: Command run after the session ends. Skipped when its `do` failed (it never took effect).

Preset.description:
A named bundle of the fields below. `Custom` (the default) means the explicit fields rule; any
other preset ignores the stored fields and expands to its own ([`DisplayPolicy::effective`]).

PresetInfo.description:
One preset's human-facing description + the fields it expands to, so the console can render a
preset picker with an accurate "what this does" preview without hardcoding the expansion.

fields.description: The effective policy this preset expands to (the same fields a `custom` policy carries).

summary.description: One-line story shown next to the option.

detect.description:
How to recognize this title's process — see [`CustomEntry::detect`]. A provider that knows its
titles' install directories (Playnite does) should send them: it is what lets a game launched
through the provider's own client still end its session when the player quits.

external_id.description: The provider's stable id for this title (the reconcile diff key).

icon.description:
Which brand mark to draw — see [`GameEntry::icon`]. This is the field a library plugin sets
on its `launchers(cfg)` tiles, and the whole reason the token exists.

prep.description: Per-title prep/undo steps — commands run as the host user; operator-privileged config.

role.description:
Whether this entry is a game or the launcher itself — see [`GameRole`]. A library plugin
emits its `launchers(cfg)` entries with `role: "launcher"`.

ProviderEntryInput.description:
One title in a provider's declarative reconcile payload (RFC §8): [`CustomInput`] plus the
provider's required stable key.

ProviderRemoved.description: The count envelope a provider uninstall returns.

removed.description: How many entries the provider owned (and were removed).

ProviderRunningAccepted.description: The result of a liveness report.

matched.description: How many reported titles matched an entry this provider currently publishes.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds this report stays authoritative without being restated — re-report inside it while
anything is running.

unknown.description: How many were ignored because no such entry exists (a report that raced a reconcile).

running.description:
Every title of this provider's that is running **right now**. The full set, not a delta:
anything absent from it is reported as stopped.

slot.description: Slot to release (see `state`); omit to release **all** kept displays.

released.description: Number of kept displays torn down.

Remedy.description:
What the operator should do about it. Always copy-paste — the host runs unprivileged and the
console must never trigger privileged mutation. The `punktfunk` group in particular is
deliberately opt-in: writing the vhci `attach` node materialises arbitrary emulated USB devices
(security review 2026-08-05, M-4), so joining it stays a deliberate act with the caveat attached.

command.description: A single pasteable shell command, when one fixes it outright.

relogin_required.description:
True when the fix only takes effect after logging out and back in — a `systemd --user`
manager keeps the supplementary group set it started with. This distinction is the
difference between "I already added myself!" and a working virtual pad.

text.description: Plain-language instruction. English fallback — the console overrides it by check id.

RenameClient.description: Body of `PATCH /clients/{fingerprint}` — the device's display name.

label.description:
The name to show for this device. `null` (or an empty/whitespace-only string) clears it and
the device goes back to being listed by fingerprint alone.

Scrubbed before storage by the same sanitizer the native plane runs on device names:
control characters and Unicode bidi overrides are stripped (they could make one paired
device impersonate another in this very list), whitespace collapsed, and the result capped
at 64 characters.

RunningTitle.description: One running title in a provider's liveness report.

external_id.description: The provider's own stable id for the title — the same key its reconcile payload uses.

pid.description:
The process id the provider started for it, when it knows one. Optional, and never trusted
as a bare number: the host re-resolves it and pins it to its start time before it is ever
signalled, so a stale or recycled pid simply contributes nothing.

RuntimeStatus.description: Live host status (changes as clients launch/end sessions).

active_sessions.description:
Number of live streaming sessions across BOTH planes (GameStream + native punktfunk/1). The
native server admits concurrent sessions, so this can exceed 1; `session`/`stream` below
describe a single representative session for the detail card.

oneOf.description:
The audio wiring verdict (Windows hosts; absent on other platforms and before the first
wiring pass). Present even while idle — the wiring exists for the host's lifetime.

audio_streaming.description: True while the audio stream thread is running.

games.description:
Every launched game the host is tracking: one row per live session that launched a title, plus
any game whose session has ended and which is waiting out its reconnect window before being
ended (`state: "grace"`). Empty when nothing was launched — a plain desktop stream has no game.

native_paired_clients.description:
Number of paired native (punktfunk/1) devices — the default plane, so on a host that has
never been touched by Moonlight this is the only non-zero one of the pair.

paired_clients.description:
Number of pinned (paired) GameStream client certificates. Native (punktfunk/1) devices pair
against a separate store and are counted in `native_paired_clients` — sum the two for
"how many clients are paired with this host".

pin_pending.description:
True while a pairing handshake is parked waiting for the user's PIN
(submit it via `POST /api/v1/pair/pin`).

oneOf.description:
A representative active session. GameStream's launch (Moonlight `/launch`) when present, else
the first live native session. `null` when nothing is streaming.

The active stream's parameters — RTSP-negotiated for GameStream, or the live native session's
mode/codec/bitrate. `null` when nothing is streaming.

video_streaming.description: True while the video stream thread is running.

installed.description: Is the runner payload/unit present at all?

principal.description: Windows: the account the task runs as.

ScannerInfo.description:
One **game source** on this host, with its enable state — the unit the console renders a toggle
for. A source is either a scanner compiled into this build or a plugin that reconciles entries in
(WP2.6); the console treats them identically, which is what makes the extraction invisible.

enabled.description: Whether this host runs the source (default true).

entries.description:
How many entries this source currently contributes. `None` for a built-in scanner, whose
count would mean walking every launcher's files just to render a toggle.

id.description:
Stable source id — the same string this source's entries carry in their `store` field. For a
plugin source it is also its provider id and its store claim: one string, by construction, so
a user's disabled state survives a built-in scanner being replaced by its plugin.

label.description: Human-facing name for the console toggle.

origin.description:
Where the source comes from. Always `plugin` from this host build onward — see
[`SourceOrigin`].

provider.description: The provider id backing a `plugin` source — absent for a built-in scanner.

enabled.description: Whether this source should contribute titles on this host.

SessionInfo.description: Client-requested launch parameters (key material is never exposed here).

SessionRef.description: A live A/V session (the plane-neutral notion the Dashboard shows).

client.description: Short client label (cert-fingerprint prefix, or peer IP for an anonymous client).

id.description: Host-local session id (unique within this host process).

disconnect_grace_seconds.description:
How long a vanished client has to reconnect before `Always` ends its game. Ignored by the
other two policies.

game_on_new_launch.description: End this client's previous game when it launches a different one. See [`GameOnNewLaunch`].

game_on_session_end.description: End the launched game when the session ends. See [`GameOnSessionEnd`].

session_on_game_exit.description: End the streaming session when the launched game exits.

SessionSettingsState.description: The session⇄game lifetime settings, plus which axes this build acts on.

configured.description: Whether an operator has ever saved these settings (`false` ⇒ `settings` are the defaults).

enforced.description:
Which fields this build actually enforces. Empty on a platform with no launch path (macOS),
so the console can say so instead of offering a switch that does nothing.

settings.description: The stored settings (or the built-in defaults when this host has never been configured).

gpu_id.description:
Required when `mode` is `manual`: the stable `id` of a currently listed GPU
(see `listGpus`).

mode.description: `auto` (env pin, else max dedicated VRAM — the default) or `manual`.

Severity.description:
How much a non-ok status matters. Orthogonal to [`CheckStatus`] on purpose: a check can be
`warn` about something `critical` (degraded, not dead) and the console sorts by both.

public_key.description: `ed25519:<base64>`. Omitted ⇒ an unsigned source (accepted, flagged everywhere).

SourceView.description: A configured catalog source and how its last refresh went.

builtin.description:
The built-in `unom` source: not editable, not removable, and the only source whose entries
may carry the "verified" tier.

error.description: Why the last refresh failed, if it did.

fetched_at.description: Unix seconds of the data we hold, when we hold any.

signed.description:
Whether we check a signature on this source's index. An unsigned source still works; the
console marks it.

stale.description:
The catalog we're serving is older than the last refresh attempt (offline, or the last
fetch failed) — entries still install, because the pin travelled with the entry.

StageTiming.description: One pipeline stage's latency in an aggregation window (microseconds).

StatsSample.description: One aggregated sample (~ every 2 s native, ~ every 1 s GameStream).

fps.description: Genuine NEW frames/s from the source.

mbps.description:
Attempted sealed wire bytes/s (Mb/s): full UDP payloads at seal time — video AU bytes
plus shard framing (header + AEAD) plus FEC parity, and for PyroWave's datagram-aligned
mode the zero-padded window tails. NOT goodput, and NOT reduced by socket send drops.

packets_dropped.description: Packets dropped this window (receiver-side / reassembler, where known).

send_dropped.description: Host send-buffer overflow / EAGAIN this window (delta).

stages.description: Ordered pipeline stages for this path.

t_ms.description: Milliseconds since capture start (monotonic; stamped by [`StatsRecorder::push_sample`]).

StatsStatus.description: Snapshot of the in-progress capture for the management API.

elapsed_ms.description:
Host-measured elapsed time of the in-progress capture, in ms (`0` if idle). Computed from the
host's MONOTONIC clock, so a console can show elapsed time without subtracting `started_unix_ms`
from its own (possibly skewed) wall clock.

kind.description: Path of the in-progress capture (`""` if idle).

started_unix_ms.description: Unix start time of the in-progress capture (`0` if idle).

last_resize_ms.description:
Most recent mid-stream resize total, reconfigure → pipeline rebuilt, in ms (native sessions;
`null` when no resize happened / GameStream).

min_fec.description: Client's parity floor per FEC block (`minRequiredFecPackets`).

time_to_first_frame_ms.description:
Session bring-up total, hello → first video packet, in ms (native sessions; `null` on the
GameStream plane or while the session is still bringing up).

StreamRef.description: A live video stream (what the stream marker file reflects).

app.description:
The launched app/title for this stream, when one was requested (store-qualified id on
the native plane, app title on the GameStream plane).

client.description: Client-supplied device name; may be empty.

SubmitPin.description: The PIN Moonlight displays during pairing.

Topology.description: What the host does to the box's display topology while managed virtual displays are up.

UiCredential.description:
`GET /plugins/{id}/ui-credential` — the console proxy's server-side lookup (bearer + loopback).
This is the only endpoint that returns a secret; the console BFF denylists it from the browser.

UnpairAllResult.description:
What a bulk unpair removed. Shared by the two collection DELETEs (`/clients` and
`/native/clients`) so the console sees one schema across both pairing planes.

A count rather than 204: "unpair everything" is idempotent, so an empty store is a success, and
the operator still wants to be told whether that meant three devices or none.

unpaired.description: Clients removed from the trust store — 0 when nothing was paired.

UpdateJobInfo.description: A running apply job (or a spawned installer that hasn't resolved yet).

UpdateManifestInfo.description: One channel's manifest facts, as much as the console renders.

notes_url.description: Release-notes link (pinned to our forge by the manifest validator).

serial.description: Publish serial (unix seconds) — monotonic per channel.

stale.description: The last verified manifest is suspiciously old (>45 days) — the freeze/stale hint.

version.description: The released version this manifest announces.

UpdateNativeAccess.description:
PATCH body for a paired device's access (the console edit sheet: change the preset, extend,
"expire now", make permanent). **Partial**: an omitted `grants` keeps the current grants, and
omitted expiry fields keep the current expiry — send only what changes.

clear_expiry.description:
`true` removes the expiry — access becomes permanent. Mutually exclusive with
`expires_in_secs` (400).

expires_in_secs.description:
New expiry in seconds **from now** (relative; the host stores the absolute deadline).
`0` expires the device now. Omit to keep the current expiry. Mutually exclusive with
`clear_expiry` (400).

grants.description:
New grant bitmask (`GRANT_*` bits 0–5); reserved bits are a 400. Omit to keep the
device's current grants.

UpdateResultInfo.description: Durable outcome of the most recent apply attempt (survives the host's own restart).

log_path.description: The installer's own log file on this host, for diagnosis.

stage.description: The stage that failed; absent on success.

staged.description: Applied but activates on the next reboot (rpm-ostree).

UpdateStatus.description: The full update-check state for this host.

apply.description:
What the console may offer for this install: `notify` (show the command) — later
phases add `full` (one-click apply) and `staged` (apply + reboot to finish).

available.description:
A newer release than `current_version` exists for this channel (definitive
comparisons only — an unparseable version pair never flags).

channel_hint.description: The copy-pastable update command for this install kind.

check_disabled.description: Update checks are disabled on this host (`PUNKTFUNK_UPDATE_CHECK=0`).

oneOf.description: The apply in flight, if any.

last_checked_unix.description: When the last successful check happened (unix seconds).

last_error.description: Why the last check failed, verbatim, if it did.

oneOf.description: Outcome of the most recent apply attempt.
The last verified manifest, if any check has succeeded.

not_published.description:
The check reached the feed and found this channel has **no release published yet** —
an expected state (a channel nobody has announced to answers with a 404), not a
failure. Mutually exclusive with `last_error`, so a UI can say "nothing published yet"
instead of painting an empty feed as a broken host. Never set once a manifest has been
seen for this channel: a feed that loses a document it used to serve stays an error.

opt_in_hint.description:
This install could one-click apply, but the operator hasn't opted in yet — the
command to run (Linux: join the `punktfunk-update` group).
